scope: Disposition of legacy Ruby facade and native module methods; not a typed API baseline or a parity claim.

groups.replacement: Typed common JSON analyze/diff2/merge2/merge3 operations with TreeHaver-owned parser registration and Rust-owned decisions.
groups.gap: Local Ruby JSON provider no longer inherits the prototype adapter or performs Ruby diff comparisons/text lookup. Complete core evidence is projected into portable Ruby values. All 93 JSON examples pass against the installed core artifact, including native semantic comparisons. JSON Pointer identities, root/document subjects and strict constraint rejection are intentional compatibility changes. Broader golden-master authority, downstream, hosted/released-package and lint/coverage gates remain open; retain legacy regression evidence without publishing the prototype.

groups.replacement: Typed analyze and diff2 operations in structuredmerge-core, using TreeHaver and Rust-owned family analysis/matching.
groups.gap: JSON has migrated separately. Remaining family adapters still compute diff2 from owner maps and must move those decisions into Rust. parse_sources alone is syntax transport, not analysis.

groups.replacement: Typed directional merge2 and base-aware merge3 request/result envelopes calling the existing family kernels.
groups.gap: JSON has migrated separately. Remaining family engines and their Ruby adapters still need typed orchestration and parity review. Preserve current/incoming direction, dialects, conflicts, diagnostics and source evidence; do not synthesize a base for merge2 or invent unsupported operations.

groups.replacement: Typed Git merge3 report over ast-merge-git and shared core operation results.
groups.gap: Retain change classifications, render report, conflicted source and exit-policy evidence. The Ruby adapter advertises all operations but rejects analyze/diff2/merge2: capability correction is required, not invented implementations.

groups.replacement: Typed ast-crispr profile reports and explicit byte-range edit requests/results exported from structuredmerge-core.
groups.gap: Local Ruby main now uses typed reports and explicit edits, with request normalization and legacy Hash result projection. Revalidated 51 examples against the current installed core artifact. Hosted/released-package, remaining downstream, lint/coverage and exact malformed-input message parity remain open. Neither reports nor explicit edits prove structural selection parity; retain legacy regression evidence without publishing the prototype.

groups.replacement: Typed options/profile/plan reports from ast-template through structuredmerge-core.
groups.gap: Local Ruby main now uses typed options/profile/read-only directory plans with transport normalization and legacy report projection. Revalidated 78 examples against the current installed core artifact. Hosted/released-package, remaining downstream and lint/coverage gates remain open. Report generation is not template execution or filesystem apply; Ruby apply behavior is retained.

groups.replacement: Typed ParserHost registration, TreeHaver selection and parse_sources; explicit Rust TSLP provider registration and typed normalized results.
groups.gap: Ruby TreeHaver now registers and parses through typed structuredmerge-core, including a versioned native extra-node flag; its full 90-example suite passes against the installed core gem. Provider identity and diagnostic wording intentionally follow typed results. Hosted/released-package, downstream and full lint/coverage gates remain open. Legacy facade regression specs are retained, not migrated implementations of replace/list/probe/bulk-clear. Those lifecycle methods still need explicit disposition/contracts before facade deletion; matching method names are not drop-in compatibility.

groups.replacement: Typed capability manifest and provider identity with observable availability, support and default authority.
groups.gap: native_merge_profiles is static scope introspection, not registry negotiation or a full manifest.

groups.replacement: Typed WorkflowHost coarse callbacks with explicit host-owned workflow boundaries; Rust retains merge semantics.
groups.gap: No typed WorkflowHost currently exported. Retain boundary regressions, not a separately released host product. Consumer discovery beyond the listed local evidence remains open.

groups.replacement: Real typed-operation lifecycle tests, OperationControl and generated runtime-affine callback infrastructure; no identity-worker product API by default.
groups.gap: Some GC, concurrency, cancellation and deadline cases are migrated. Shutdown, foreign-thread entry and broad stress remain open; do not remove legacy evidence before equivalent coverage.
